readings_ruling: The dispatch asked five things. All check out, with two small precision points (findings 1 and 2). (1) PseudoLongueurCorpsConvexeLiteral n (Prop2Literal.lean:166) is the strict PseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted n (Hilbert.lean:1525) with exactly one change. The last clause `hilbertLength K A B = 0 ↔ A = B` becomes `hilbertLength K A B = 0 → A = B`. I checked this with #print on both definitions. Their bodies match token for token: the same quantification over every K with IsCorpsConvexeS n K, the same projective-measure clause for every segment Sg and every pair F ≠ F′ with lineThrough A B ∩ frontier K = {F, F′}, and the same continuity into EReal. That last clause is the literal sense of « ne s'annule que sur la diagonale » (l.312): the zeros lie on the diagonal. It is neither weaker nor stronger. pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe_literal (l.143) has the signature ∀ {n} {K}, IsCorpsConvexeS n K → … (#check), so it carries no [NeZero n]. All five inputs are NeZero-free, or the term would not elaborate with a variable n. (2) pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted_iff_literal (Printed n ↔ Literal n ∧ 0 < n) is correct. It follows from pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted_iff and pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexeLiteral_holds. As a relation between truth values it says no more than pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted_iff (finding 2). (3) « Vacuous at n = 0 » is right. S(0) = S(ℝ¹) has two antipodal points (S0_eq_or_eq_neg), and a strict convex part never holds both x and −x (neg_notMem). So the interior of a convex body of S(0) is a subsingleton (subsingleton_corpsInterior_dim_zero), and since IsCorpsConvexeS requires a nonempty interior it is exactly one point. Clauses 1 and 4 quantify over A ≠ B and have no instance. Clause 2 has only A = B instances, and there its hypothesis lineThrough A A ∩ frontier K = {F, F′}, F ≠ F′ is unsatisfiable in every dimension: lineThrough A A ⊆ {A, −A}, A is interior and −A ∉ K. This is the by_cases at the head of pseudoLength_eq_projMeasure. Clause 3 is continuity on a point. Clause 0 is not vacuous at n = 0, but it is the segment-uniqueness preamble, not one of the printed assertions. (4) stdCorpsConvexe n = Sphere.ofCone {v | ∀ i, |v i| ≤ v 0} is a genuine convex body in the strict sense. isCorpsConvexeS_stdCorpsConvexe proves IsCorpsConvexeS n (stdCorpsConvexe n) for every n, with the strict Déf. 11 predicate (IsStrictConvexPart ∧ IsCompact ∧ interior nonempty, #print), accepted as Déf. 11 by the T-bz-c2-hilbert audit. Its interior contains the open cone 0 < v₀, |vᵢ₊₁| < v₀. For n ≥ 1, exists_ne_corpsInterior_iff exhibits two distinct interior points, e₀ and e₀ + ½ e₁, so the A ≠ B clauses are satisfiable and the theorem has content. For n = 0 the body is the ray of e₀. (5) The « fonction continue » [0, +∞] reading is the strict library's existing convention, not a new one. Mesure.lean:299 defines pseudoLength : EReal as ⨅ over the majorising k, which is ⊤ for an empty set. Its checklist (Mesure.lean:53) records this as Déf. 3's reading. The strict pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe and PseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted both state Continuous into EReal, and continuous_hilbertLength_toReal gives the real form only for n ≥ 1. The file adopts that convention and states no new one. Its question 2 rightly points out that the convention decides the n = 0 case when the function is taken to be real-valued.

labels.notes: The label is correctly UNMARKED and the status is partial, as dispatched: the mark waits on OQ-56. I read the statement against l.306–313 and the scan (PDF p. 23, text layer: « qui ne s'annule que sur la diagonale », « dépendent continûment de A, B »). Hypotheses: IsCorpsConvexeS n K (Déf. 11) and V = corpsInterior K with Mathlib's charted structure on an open set. These are the paper's « V̄ un corps convexe de S(n) d'intérieur V », as in the audited strict assembly. No other hypothesis is added, and in particular no [NeZero n]. Conclusions: (0) the unique segment, so l_V = hilbertLength K. (1) For A ≠ B, F ≠ F′ exist with lineThrough A B ∩ frontier K = {F, F′}, plus A, B ∈ )F, F′(, a strengthening disclosed as such. (2) For every segment and every such pair, pseudoLength = projMeasure F A B F′, both labellings covered. (3) Continuous on V × V into EReal. (4) `= 0 → A = B`. So under the literal reading of OQ-56 the theorem is at least the paper's, in every dimension. Under the « iff » reading it is weaker by exactly l_V(A, A) = 0, which the file says (SCOPE bullet 3), and the strict pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe stays the n ≥ 1 candidate. The printed-format Prop is assertions (2)–(4) only, like the strict Printed form. So under a literal ruling the anchor should be the theorem (it carries clause 1, the existence of F, F′, which the paper presupposes), not the Prop. The REPORT's routing names the theorem. Auxiliary statements checked. hilbertLength_eq_zero_iff_and_pos: for a fixed K, l = 0 ↔ A = B ∧ 0 < n. hilbertLength_ne_top_iff_pos: l finite everywhere on V × V ↔ 0 < n, using hK's nonempty interior at n = 0. subsingleton_corpsInterior_dim_zero. exists_ne_corpsInterior_iff. All four are stated as described. The REPORT's three findings hold. (i) Vacuous at n = 0: readings_ruling 3, with the clause-2 precision of finding 1. (ii) Not real-valued at n = 0: l_V(A, A) = ⊤ (hilbertLength_self_dim_zero), so under a real-valued reading of « fonction continue » the literal form also fails at n = 0. This is conditional on Déf. 1/Déf. 3 giving coincident points no measure, which is OQ-45, and is stated as such. (iii) The planner's [r] that clause 0 might need n ≥ 1 is false. isProjSegment_corpsInterior_iff is used by the NeZero-free theorem, so it carries no NeZero. The closer's register remark is also right. OQ-56 (registers/DECISIONS.md:212) cites « (l.306–310) » for the phrase, which is at l.312, outside that range. The transcription's other line references in the docstring (l.232, l.249–251, l.297–298, l.303, l.306–313, l.312, l.315–317) are all correct.
